action_1_desc.sample: Move ₹10 lakh of the deposit book into the retirement portfolio as a lumpsum.

action_2_desc.sample: The ₹21,700 surplus as a SIP plus ₹10 lakh from the FD book adds ₹0.81 crore by 2036.

action_3_desc.sample: Every ₹10,000 a month trimmed today lowers the corpus required by about ₹42 lakh.

action_4_desc.sample: A third property yields 2.6% and pushes real estate past 50%. Defer it.

action_5_desc.sample: Bring property from 40% of assets towards 30% over the next five years.

action_6_desc.sample: ₹5 lakh prepaid with a 5% EMI step-up closes the loan in 2034, saving ₹11.2 lakh.

action_6_title.sample: Home loan — prepay, don’t top up

allocation_comment.sample: Two-fifths of the balance sheet sits in property, which cannot be drawn on goal by goal. The plan therefore funds every goal from the remaining ₹2.17 crore of financial assets and shifts new savings towards that side of the sheet.

annuity_comment.sample: A flat withdrawal plan fails by the mid-2050s. The corpus has to keep a growth allocation through retirement, which is what the core-and-satellite structure is for.

bucket_retirement_desc.sample: EPF, PPF, NPS and SSY are pure long-lock assets. At ten years from retirement, a 26% allocation here is healthy and needs no addition beyond the statutory flows.

cashflow_comment.sample: A 49% savings rate is the single strongest number in this plan — it is what makes retirement at 55 discussable at all. The unallocated ₹21,700 is deliberately left free; it absorbs a bad month before any goal has to be paused.

corpus_later_2_label.sample: Other asset class — second property, if monetised

cover_ci_status.sample: Gap. A ₹25 L rider pays a lump sum on diagnosis.

cover_classification_comment.sample: Mixing cover with investment is what makes protection expensive. Keeping the three jobs separate — term for income, floater and top-up for health, riders for illness — buys far more cover for the same ₹1.35 lakh a year.

cover_debt_note.sample: Home and car loans come off the top before anything is left.

cover_endowment_status.sample: ₹9.6 L maturing 2032, returning about 4.6% a year.

cover_floater_status.sample: ₹10 L shared across all four members, in force.

cover_gap_comment.sample: Cover is sized to what the family would have to replace, not to what feels affordable. Ten times income clears the loans, funds both children's education and leaves Aditi an income for the years the salary would have covered.

cover_gap_headline.sample: Life cover stands at 4.2 times income, against the ten times this family needs

cover_gap_note.sample: Enough to fund the family for roughly seventeen years.

cover_pa_status.sample: ₹50 L on accidental death or disability, in force.

cover_suggestion_comment.sample: The endowment stays until it matures in 2032, so nothing already paid is lost. Its ₹51,000 renewal is simply not repeated: ₹42,000 of it buys the additional term cover and ₹9,000 buys the health top-up.

cover_suggestion_headline.sample: The same ₹1.35 lakh premium can buy 2.4 times the cover it buys today

cover_term_status.sample: ₹1.5 Cr on Rohan and ₹75 L on Aditi, both in force.

cover_topup_status.sample: Gap. ₹25 L above the ₹10 L limit costs about ₹9,000 a year.

cover_ulip_status.sample: Not held; charges dilute cover and returns alike.

cover_waiver_status.sample: Add at renewal. Keeps every policy alive if income stops.

deposit_book_note.sample: Held in fixed deposits earning about 5.3% after tax — nineteen months of household expenses, where twelve is the agreed reserve.

deposit_prepay_note.sample: Earns 8.4% risk-free by cancelling interest; saves ₹11.2 L.

deposit_reserve_note.sample: Twelve months of expenses at ₹1.5 L a month, untouched.

deposit_retirement_note.sample: Grows at an expected 10-11% instead of 5.3% after tax.

emi_crossover_note.sample: Principal overtakes interest only six years from now.

emi_interest_note.sample: Every month of delay costs ₹26,600 in interest alone.

emi_prepay_note.sample: Prepayment attacks principal directly, so the crossover arrives three years sooner.

emi_split_comment.sample: An EMI is not a fixed cost split evenly over the years. In the early years it is mostly rent on the borrowed money, which is why a prepayment made now is worth several times the same amount paid in 2034.

emi_split_headline.sample: ₹26,600 of today's ₹42,500 EMI is interest — only ₹15,900 reduces the loan

equity_comment.sample: Individual stock selection needs continuous research, and a single-stock failure this close to retirement is difficult to recover from. Staging the exit over four years keeps the capital gains tax bill near zero.

equity_description.sample: Eleven holdings built up over fifteen years. Four of them account for 58% of the book, and two sectors account for two- thirds of it.

equity_recommendation.sample: Move the seven smallest holdings into diversified funds over four financial years, using the ₹1.25 lakh annual exemption. Keep the four convictions you actively follow.

fd_2_remarks.sample: Reallocate on maturity to the retirement portfolio

fd_3_remarks.sample: Retain — part of the emergency reserve

fd_4_remarks.sample: AAA rated; carried into the retirement bucket

fd_5_remarks.sample: Retain — part of the emergency reserve

fd_comment.sample: At ₹1.5 lakh of monthly expenses, ₹28 lakh is about nineteen months of cover; twelve is comfortable. After tax these deposits earn about 5.3% against 6% inflation, so roughly ₹10 lakh should move out of deposits and into the retirement portfolio as a lumpsum.

freed_cashflow_comment.sample: Each instalment is re-tagged the month it is freed rather than absorbed into spending. This is what lifts the retirement contribution six-fold in the last two years before 2036, and it is the cheapest ₹0.75 crore available to the plan.

goal4_comment.sample: Move this corpus out of equity in stages from 2032 — a third a year — so that a poor market in 2034 cannot delay the build. The ₹26 lakh surplus is deliberate: construction overruns are the norm, not the exception.

goal4_intro.sample: Built without a construction loan. The home loan closes in 2033 precisely so that no new debt is taken on a year later.

goal4_margin.sample: ₹26 L clear — the contingency on a build

goal4_redirect_label.sample: From April 2034 the combined ₹93,000 redirects to

goal_comment.sample: Book the trip out of this corpus and nothing else. Funding a discretionary goal from the education or retirement pots is how a well-built plan quietly drifts.

goal_intro.sample: Held in arbitrage and short-duration debt funds. At a two-year horizon the priority is that the money is intact in 2028, not that it grows.

goal_redirect_label.sample: From April 2028 the ₹20,000 SIP redirects to

goal_src2_terms.sample: ₹5.50 L from the FD book · 7% · matures 2028

goals_funding_intro.sample: Eight goals, in the order the money is needed. Each slide states the target in the year it falls due, and the exact sources that meet it.

goals_section_intro.sample: Eight goals over eighteen years, mapped against the ₹3 lakh a month you already invest — and against every instalment that comes free along the way.

health_summary.sample: Your current financial health is stable, with a score of 78%. The portfolio is adequately diversified, inflows are strong and every near-term goal is already funded. The score is held back by two things: 40% of the balance sheet is in property, and the plan currently depends on a single income.

home_loan_section_intro.sample: Seven years in, ₹36 lakh has left your account, and ₹38 lakh is still outstanding. This section shows why — and what a single ₹5 lakh decision changes.

investment_allocation_comment.sample: Of the ₹2.20 lakh committed each month, the ₹30,000 tagged to retirement is funded by the FD reallocation rather than by fresh saving. Property is excluded here because it cannot be drawn on goal by goal.

ladder_comment.sample: Nothing here asks the family to spend less. Each step is money already leaving the account as an EMI or a goal contribution; the discipline is simply to redirect it on the day it is freed rather than let it be absorbed.

ladder_headline.sample: Every instalment that ends is re-tagged, lifting the retirement SIP six-fold by 2035

legacy_comment.sample: The surplus above the corpus requirement is what makes legacy planning relevant here rather than theoretical. None of these four items costs more than a day, and all four fail expensively if left undone.

legacy_nominations_note.sample: Refresh nominees on EPF, PPF, NPS, all folios and both term policies; three still name a parent.

legacy_nps_note.sample: ₹1.35 crore matures in 2041. Deferred annuity for the second half of retirement or left as legacy.

legacy_records_note.sample: One consolidated statement of holdings, policies and access, shared with your spouse and reviewed yearly.

legacy_will_note.sample: Not yet drawn. With two properties and two minor children, a registered will is the priority action.

loan_1_comment.sample: At 8.4% the loan costs more than the post-tax return on your deposits, so prepaying from the FD surplus is the better use of that money. Closing in 2034 also frees the EMI before retirement.

loan_2_comment.sample: The car loan is the costliest debt on the sheet but the smallest. Clearing it from the monthly surplus rather than from the deposit book keeps the emergency reserve intact, and the freed EMI of ₹15,800 becomes part of the retirement SIP from 2029.

loan_life_continue_note.sample: ₹66.3 L still to pay, of which ₹27.4 L is interest

loan_life_footnote.sample: Loan start year, original principal and amount paid to date are derived from the stated EMI of ₹42,500, the 8.40% rate and the 2039 closing year; outstanding, interest and prepayment figures are as confirmed at review.

loan_life_headline.sample: Seven years in, the loan is only a quarter repaid — prepaying now ends it in 2034

loan_life_prepay_label.sample: WITH ₹5 LAKH PREPAID IN 2026 AND A 5% EMI STEP-UP

marriage_comment.sample: Keep this corpus in a separate folio from the retirement pot. Once withdrawals begin in 2037 it becomes very difficult to tell one pool from the other, and the marriage money is the first thing to be quietly consumed.

marriage_intro.sample: A conditional goal. If the children marry later, or more modestly, the corpus returns to the retirement pool rather than being spent because it exists.

next_step.sample: Authorise the ₹5 lakh prepayment this quarter and submit the term-cover application before the next policy renewal.

nps_comment.sample: The five-year gap between retiring at 55 and NPS maturing at 60 is bridged entirely by the mutual fund corpus. That is planned for on the withdrawal slides and needs no separate provision.

nps_description.sample: Market-linked and low-cost, with an additional ₹50,000 deduction. It matures at 60, not at 55 — so it funds the second phase of retirement rather than the first.

nps_recommendation.sample: Treat NPS as deferred corpus: counted in the lifetime total, but drawn as income from 2042, not available in 2037. Shift towards the C and G tiers from 2039 so the maturity value is not set by one bad market year.

outcome_goals_note.sample: Retirement, both educations and the renovation are each funded by a named cash flow, not by whatever is left over.

outcome_loan_note.sample: Debt-free in 2034 instead of 2039, with ₹11.7 L of interest never paid across both loans.

outcome_protection_note.sample: Life cover rises from 4.2× to 10× income and health cover from ₹10 L to ₹35 L, on the same premium.

outcomes_comment.sample: The ₹21,700 monthly surplus and the ₹10 lakh released from deposits add about ₹0.81 crore by 2036. That is what carries the corpus past the ₹6.25 crore the retirement income needs.

outcomes_headline.sample: The three moves together turn a ₹0.75 crore retirement shortfall into a small surplus

pf_comment.sample: At 8.1% the PF balance roughly doubles every nine years with no market risk. If the declared rate falls below 7.5%, the case for the voluntary top-up weakens against equity over an eleven-year horizon.

pf_description.sample: Employer and employee contribute together each month. Interest is declared annually, the maturity is tax-free, and the balance compounds untouched until you leave employment.

pf_recommendation.sample: Transfer, never withdraw, on a job change. Leave the balance to compound to 2037, then move it into the debt core of the retirement portfolio.

pf_value_note.sample: 20% of the total corpus, entirely tax-free

pg_1_basis.sample: ₹45 L today, at 10% over 10 years — a two-year course abroad

pg_2_basis.sample: ₹45 L today, at 10% over 15 years — four years after retirement

pg_comment.sample: Ira’s postgraduate year falls four years into retirement. It is funded from its own corpus, not from the retirement pot — that separation is deliberate and should be maintained even if markets are strong in 2037.

policies_comment.sample: Annual premium is ₹1.35 lakh, of which ₹51,000 buys very little cover. Life cover is 4.2× annual income against a 10× benchmark, and ₹10 lakh of health cover for four is thin.

policy_1_remarks.sample: Raise towards ₹5 Cr — cover is 4.2× annual income

policy_2_remarks.sample: Top up to ₹1 Cr when the second income restarts

policy_3_remarks.sample: Add a ₹25 L super top-up this year

policy_4_remarks.sample: Effective return ~4.6%; hold to maturity, do not renew

ppf_comment.sample: Contributing on the fifth of April rather than in March adds roughly ₹2.4 lakh over the eleven years, for no extra money. It is the cheapest improvement in this deck.

ppf_description.sample: A voluntary, government-backed account with a fifteen-year term, extendable in five-year blocks. Contributions, interest and maturity are all tax-free.

ppf_recommendation.sample: Fund both accounts before the fifth of April each year so the full balance earns interest for the whole year. Extend rather than close at maturity.

ppf_value_note.sample: Tax-free, and available in full from 2037

prepay_end_note.sample: the loan ends in 2034, two years before retirement

prepay_funding_comment.sample: The reserve stays fully intact at twelve months. Only the excess above it is put to work, so the family takes on no additional risk and gives up no liquidity it actually needs. The ₹2 lakh car-loan prepayment comes from monthly surplus, not from this pool.

prepay_funding_headline.sample: The prepayment comes from idle deposits, not from the family's monthly budget

prepay_impact_comment.sample: The deposits behind the prepayment earn about 5.3% after tax while the loan charges 8.4%. Moving ₹5 lakh across that gap is the single highest-certainty return available in the plan, and it needs no market view.

prepay_impact_headline.sample: ₹5 lakh prepaid today removes ₹11.2 lakh of interest and five years of EMI

prepay_return_note.sample: a 224% return on the ₹5 lakh, tax-free

protection_intro.sample: Every goal in this plan assumes ten more years of income. Protection is what makes that assumption safe to rely on.

retirement_section_intro.sample: Ten years of accumulation against thirty-five years of drawdown. Each retirement asset is projected through April 2037 on its own terms, then consolidated.

retirement_summary_1.sample: On these assumptions, retiring at 55 needs a corpus of about ₹6.25 crore to fund ₹2.06 lakh a month, inflated at 6%, to age 90. The plan currently builds ₹5.50 crore, leaving a gap of ₹0.75 crore.

retirement_summary_2.sample: Three levers close it, and any two are sufficient: directing the ₹21,700 monthly surplus into the retirement SIP and deploying the ₹10 lakh FD reallocation as a lumpsum, which together add ₹0.81 crore by 2036; working to 57 instead of 55; or monetising the second property at retirement. Once funded, a core-and-satellite structure keeps the essential income in stable assets and leaves the satellite free for growth and legacy planning.

sip_comment.sample: Two-thirds of the monthly commitment funds goals inside the next ten years, which is why only ₹30,000 currently reaches retirement. The redirection plan corrects that from 2029 onwards without raising the total.

ssy_comment.sample: Total contributions of ₹22.5 lakh become ₹66.5 lakh, tax-free. Half of that funds Isha’s undergraduate course in 2036 through a partial withdrawal; the balance carries to 2040.

suggestion_1_desc.sample: ₹5 lakh from the deposit book, with a 5% EMI step-up each year. The deposits earn 5.3% after tax; the loan costs 8.4%.

suggestion_2_desc.sample: Hold the endowment to maturity and stop renewing it. The same premium budget buys term cover to ₹5 crore and a ₹25 lakh health top-up.

suggestion_3_desc.sample: As each loan and goal closes, the instalment moves straight to the retirement SIP instead of into spending.

suggestions_comment.sample: None of the three needs fresh money. Each one reuses cash the household already commits every month, which is why the plan can close the retirement gap without changing the family's standard of living.

takeaway_1_desc.sample: ₹5 lakh of idle deposits removes ₹11.2 lakh of interest and five years of EMI.

takeaway_1_title.sample: The home loan ends in 2034, not 2039

takeaway_2_desc.sample: ₹1.35 lakh a year moves life cover from 4.2× to 10× income and health cover to ₹35 lakh.

takeaway_2_title.sample: Cover trebles on the same premium

takeaway_3_desc.sample: The retirement SIP steps up from ₹30,000 to ₹1.85 lakh a month by 2035.

takeaway_3_title.sample: Freed EMIs go to work, not to spending

takeaway_4_desc.sample: The corpus reaches ₹6.31 crore against ₹6.25 crore needed, with no new saving.

ug_1_basis.sample: ₹25 L today, at 10% education inflation over 6 years

ug_1_note.sample: ₹35,000 redirects to Aarav’s PG from April 2032.

ug_2_basis.sample: ₹25 L today, at 10% education inflation over 11 years

ug_2_note.sample: ₹20,000 redirects to Ira’s PG from April 2037.

ug_comment.sample: If either course is taken abroad, add rupee depreciation of roughly 3% a year on top of the 10% — that raises Aarav’s requirement to about ₹53 lakh. We will re- test this at the 2029 review, when the subject choice is clearer.
